::: {.unit unit="lp-infantry"}
The Laser trooper is Kessler-Hayashi's standard soldier: mech armor and a short-range laser rifle. Most of its raids and patrols are made of them. Once the Armory has its Warden plating, bullets do much less to them, so switch to fire or tank shells.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-tank"}
The Tank is Kessler-Hayashi's siege vehicle, and its shell is made for walls and buildings. Tanks make up most of a siege escort: they wait out of range while the mortars work, then drive in through the breach. Rocket troopers and battle tanks beat it; rifles do not.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-railgunner"}
The Railgunner is a heavy trooper with a hand-held rail cannon. It stays out of raids and defends its own camp: it guards the base and its siege guns and clears the biter nests nearby. Its slug punches through a few biters at a time and is strong against nests, but does little to walls. Some drop rail coils, which your rail rifle needs.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-laser-drone"}
The Laser drone is Kessler-Hayashi's only flier, an armored combat drone with a laser. A camp gets a few once it reaches its second level. It flies over walls, cliffs and water, and bullets do little to it. Rocket troopers and flak turrets bring it down; put the flak where it crosses your wall.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-skyguard"}
The Anti-air trooper is a Laser trooper with a tracking laser for shooting down fliers. Against ground targets it does very little, and camps field it alongside Laser troopers, never instead of them. Keep your combat robots away from it and send ground units.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-lance"}
The Heavy laser trooper carries a long laser that outranges your submachine guns and cuts through light armor. It stands back and fires. Close the distance with vehicles, or let a gun turret, which still outranges it, deal with it.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-shock"}
The Shock trooper fires an arc of lightning that jumps from target to target and stuns each one briefly. It is made for crowds, and does little to a single vehicle. The Siege works also sends them after your artillery. Keep your squads spread out.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-aegis"}
The Heavy tank is a tank with extra armor and a rail cannon. Its slug ignores armor, which makes it Kessler-Hayashi's answer to your battle tanks, but it fires too slowly to matter against troopers. Your rocket troopers outrange it, so fight it at full range.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-prism"}
The Laser tank's beam splits on the first target it hits and forks into the units around it. It is made to break massed troopers and does little to walls or lone vehicles. Send battle tanks or rocket troopers at it, not infantry.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-tesla"}
The Lightning tank carries a tesla turret's emitter. Its lightning jumps along your turret line, and every laser or tesla turret it hits stops firing for a moment. A few of them slow a laser line badly. Gun turrets and flamethrowers are not affected, so mix them into the line.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-howitzer-truck"}
The Howitzer truck is an artillery cannon on a tank hull, used to haul a siege's howitzer into position. It does not fire on the move: it drives to the site, the howitzer is set up there to shell the roboports behind your wall, and the truck pulls back. Your artillery outranges the howitzer and engages it on its own.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-hauler"}
The Hauler is a lightly armed, armored truck that carries supplies between Kessler-Hayashi's camps. It is slow and does not fight well. A squad posted on the road between camps will catch them.
:::
